sections.html:
East Chicago sits on Lake Michigan in Lake County, about 18 miles from downtown Chicago and just west of Gary. The population was 26,370 at the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate is 25,610. The city peaked at 57,669 in 1960 and has been shrinking for decades.

Renters outnumber owners here. Only 42.9% of housing is owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $105,400, and median gross rent is $854. The 2020 census counted 11,735 housing units, and 16.0% of them were vacant.

A vacant house or one that needs work should expect a buyer to order an inspection and price in repairs.

East Chicago grew up as a twin city. Indiana Harbor, the East Side, formed around Inland Steel and housed most of the mill families. The West Side was the home of the native-born business community. The older housing stock sits close to the industrial lakefront, and many of those houses are well past the age when roofs, wiring and plumbing were last updated.

Two places in the city are on the National Register of Historic Places: the Marktown Historic District and the Indiana Harbor Public Library. A house in Marktown may be subject to rules for historic properties, and buyers will ask about them.

Steel is why the city exists. Inland Steel arrived in 1903, and today Cleveland-Cliffs runs the mills as the Indiana Harbor Works. The job losses of 1974 to 1986 are a large part of why the city has so many vacant and aging houses today.

The USS Lead Superfund site is a residential area north of a former lead smelter that operated from about 1906 to 1985. The site covers about 1,200 homes, parks, schools and public buildings, and the soil there was contaminated with lead.

On October 2, 2020, EPA removed 671 cleaned-up properties from the Superfund National Priorities List and said they were cleared for residential use. Lead-contaminated soil had been removed from 95% of the 1,078 mostly residential properties in Zones 2 and 3. Properties not yet finished stayed on the list, and all Zone 1 properties remained on it until cleanup.

  • The cleanup target for soil is 400 mg/kg of lead.
  • Properties removed from the list may be eligible for the city's Residential Repair Program.
  • EPA continues to look at possible groundwater issues in the area.

If your house is in or near the site, expect buyers and their lenders to ask whether the lot was cleaned up. Check EPA's current pages for your specific address, and have any cleanup paperwork ready. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can skip the lender questions, though you should still share what you know.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house in East Chicago
sections.html:
Rental sales are a regular part of this market. The city requires owners of rental housing to register each property every year by January 31. The City Controller's office provides the form, and the city will not accept it without proof of insurance equal to the property value, or a bond or letter of credit.

A new owner must register within 30 days of obtaining title. A late fee applies to each unit not registered by April 15 each year, and failing to register is a violation with a fine per unit. Each day of violation counts as a separate offense. Call the City Controller for the current dollar amounts.

If you are selling a tenant-occupied house, confirm your registration is current first. A buyer will want a clean record, and a lapse can follow the property to the new owner.

East Chicago is in Lake County, so deeds go to the Lake County Recorder at 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor, in Crown Point. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone number is 219-755-3730. Closing companies normally record the deed for you.

Property tax goes to the Lake County Treasurer at 219-755-3760. Indiana collects in two installments, May and November. Pay up to 30 days late and a 5% penalty applies. After that it is 10%.

The county compiles its delinquent list by July 1 or 51 days after the due date, and the tax sale is held online. Anyone behind on a bill who wants to sell can ask the title company to pay the balance from the proceeds at closing. Do this before the list is built if you can.

The School City of East Chicago serves the whole city, and all residents are zoned to Central High School. Two charter options also operate here, East Chicago Urban Enterprise for kindergarten through eighth grade and East Chicago Lighthouse Charter School.

A South Shore Line station is in the city, and East Chicago Transit runs free buses on three routes: Crosstown, West Calumet and Griffith Plaza. State Road 912, the Cline Avenue Expressway, links the city to the Indiana Toll Road and the Borman Expressway. Those connections are worth listing for a buyer who commutes to Chicago.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
Many East Chicago sales involve a vacant house, a tenant situation, an estate, or a house that needs more repair than the owner can pay for. A cash buyer looks at the house as it stands and makes an offer you can read before you commit.

  • You give us the address and tell us about the condition, vacancy and any tenants.
  • We visit the house and send a written offer.
  • If you accept, a title company runs the title search and prepares the closing.
  • You pick a closing date, and any tax or lien balance is paid from your proceeds.

Without a lender there is no appraisal, so repair requests that often follow one never come up. Offers will usually sit below a fully renovated retail sale. Compare the number with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and the months a house can sit.

faqs.q: Is it hard to sell a house in the USS Lead area of East Chicago?
faqs.a: It can take longer, since buyers and lenders ask whether the property was cleaned up. EPA says 671 properties were removed from the Superfund list on October 2, 2020 and were cleared for residential use. Properties not yet finished stayed on the list.

faqs.q: When must East Chicago landlords register rental property?
faqs.a: By January 31 each year, with proof of insurance or a bond. New owners must register within 30 days of obtaining title, and a late fee applies to units not registered by April 15.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in East Chicago?
faqs.a: At the Lake County Recorder in Crown Point, 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, second floor. Call 219-755-3730 for hours and requirements.

faqs.q: How much is a typical home worth in East Chicago?
faqs.a: The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $105,400. Your own house may sit well above or below that depending on condition.

faqs.q: Can I sell my East Chicago house if it is vacant or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Vacant and damaged houses are common here, with 16.0% of housing units vacant at the 2020 census. A direct buyer who purchases as-is avoids the repair requests that often follow a lender appraisal.
